title: An AI Breakthrough Has Made Decades of Computer Science Research ‘Irrelevant’ | WIRED
body: As for Linköping’s Jonsson, he plans to revisit both his own and others’ papers that hinge on ETH being true, and believes his conference paper may eventually be salvageable through another method. He’s excited to look into the details of OpenAI’s proof and see what he can learn from it and apply it to new problems. Even though it undoes the assumptions underpinning his work, having a verdict for ETH is something he could only “dream of” before, he says. “These are exciting times,” he adds. [...] Researchers have also been overwhelmed by the volume of content now being produced, thanks to AI, including slop-level results. Midway through the interview, Husfeldt receives what he suspects to be an AI-generated 17-page paper on the consequences of the ETH result from a random Gmail account. He won’t read it: “Reading math is a very big investment of cognitive time,” he says. [...] OpenAI has directly contributed to this; earlier this month, it dumped 722 manuscripts on 400 problems on GitHub, to the annoyance of academics, who complain this makes it difficult to digest the results. Adding to the frustration were several documents that contained errors, reflecting what some mathematicians saw as a hasty rollout designed to juice the company’s planned initial public offering rather than moving the field forward. title: 7 Cybersecurity Trends to Know in 2026 | Coursera
body:
## Key takeaways

 The latest cybersecurity trends change constantly because of evolving technology like cloud storage, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things (IoT).

 The top cybersecurity trends now include protecting data for remote work, addressing machine learning attacks, and updating multi-factor authentication technology. [...] ### At a glance: What are the top three trends in the cybersecurity industry?

Here's a rundown on the top three cybersecurity trends you should know:

1. Remote work: Data is more vulnerable on networks outside the office, where IT teams typically implement the latest cybersecurity protocols.

2. AI and ML: Artificial intelligence and machine learning are making threat detection more accurate and efficient, while also powering an increasing number of cybersecurity threats. [...] Georgia Tech reports that AI-powered cyberattacks are a top risk today . The use of AI allows scammers to create more believable phishing emails that entice employees and others to release sensitive data.
